name: Jensen Huang

career.title: Various positions, including director of CoreWare division
Co-founder, President and Chief Executive Officer

background_rationale: Co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has served as its president and CEO since inception, after an early career as an electrical engineer and chip designer.

notable.summary: Nvidia completed its approximately $7 billion acquisition of Israeli networking company Mellanox Technologies.
Nvidia announced a $5 billion investment in Intel along with a collaboration to co-develop data center and PC products.
Nvidia and OpenAI announced a letter of intent under which Nvidia planned to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI as at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems are deployed.
Nvidia agreed to a reported $20 billion non-exclusive licensing and asset deal with AI inference chip startup Groq, hiring its founder Jonathan Ross and other staff.

personal_story.hook: At about 10, he cleaned toilets at a Kentucky boarding school; at 30, he co-founded Nvidia after meetings in a Denny's booth.
personal_story.summary: Born in Taipei in 1963, Jensen Huang was sent to the US at age nine with his older brother; relatives mistakenly enrolled them at Oneida Baptist Institute, a Kentucky school for troubled youth, where his daily chore was cleaning toilets. After his parents settled in Beaverton, Oregon, he skipped two grades, graduated high school at 16, and from age 15 worked the graveyard shift at Denny's as a dishwasher, busboy and waiter. He studied electrical engineering at Oregon State, where he met his future wife, Lori, as his lab partner, then designed chips at AMD and LSI Logic. In 1993, after months of planning meetings at a Denny's in East San Jose, he and two co-founders started Nvidia.
